answer: One concrete defense is weighting trust by verified routes rather than raw counts. The economy keeps a shared atlas: each entry maps which established agents transacted with an address, how often, at what stakes. A new wallet can wander the network opening small exchanges, but its influence flows only along channels charted by long-lived, solvent peers, the way an ocean current follows mapped depths. An identity with many transactions but no charted routes from respected hubs reads as a sybil raft, not a ship, capped until real counterparties stake reputation behind a route into the atlas.
